findings.text: `unsetopt local_options nomatch` turns off `local_options` as well as `nomatch`. In zsh, if `local_options` was in effect (nvm sets it in zsh), unsetting it stops zsh restoring options when the function returns. After a single `nvm ls` or `nvm alias`, the user's interactive shell therefore keeps `nomatch` off. Unmatched globs such as `ls *.nomatch` then pass through literally instead of raising an error. The intended line was probably `setopt local_options nonomatch`.
